name: MAX30102EFD+T
title: Pulse oximeter and heart-rate sensor module with red and IR LEDs and I2C output
summary: MAX30102 is a reflective optical module for heart rate and blood-oxygen (SpO2) measurement. One 14-pin package holds a 660 nm red LED, an 880 nm IR LED, a photodiode, cover glass, LED drivers, ambient light cancellation, an 18-bit sigma-delta ADC, a die temperature sensor and a 32-sample FIFO. The logic runs from 1.8 V and the LEDs from a separate 3.3 V (3.1 V to 5.0 V) rail; the host reads it over I2C at up to 400 kHz, with an open-drain interrupt. A software shutdown drops supply current to 0.7 µA typical.
key_figures: 600 µA typ, SpO2 and HR mode, PW = 215 µs, 50 sps
14-pin OESIP, 5.6 mm x 3.3 mm x 1.55 mm, 0.8 mm pitch

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The module on its two rails with a host on I2C. A +3.3 V rail able to source 200 mA feeds both VLED+ pins, bypassed by 10 µF and 0.1 µF to PGND; a +1.8 V rail of 20 mA feeds VDD, bypassed by 4.7 µF and 0.1 µF to GND. SCL, SDA and the open-drain INT each have a 1 kΩ pull-up to the host's I/O rail VDDIO. The six N.C. pins are left open.
notes: U1.9 and U1.10 are the two VLED+ pins; U1.1, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 14 are the N.C. pins.

operation.text: The red (660 nm) and IR (880 nm) LEDs are pulsed by internal drivers; light returning from the skin reaches one photodiode. The SpO2 front end has ambient light cancellation built on a track-and-hold, which removes up to 200 µA of ambient photocurrent, then a continuous-time oversampling sigma-delta ADC of 18 bits with a 10.24 MHz sampling rate and a proprietary discrete-time filter. ADC full scale is selectable from 2 µA to 16 µA, and the output rate from 50 sps to 3200 sps. Results go into a 32-sample FIFO.

MODE[2:0] picks the operating state: 010 is heart-rate mode (red LED only), 011 is SpO2 mode (red and IR), 111 is multi-LED mode, where SLOT1 to SLOT4 in registers 0x11 and 0x12 say which LED fires in each time slot. Other codes are not used. Changing mode leaves every other setting and the stored data alone. Slots are enabled in order: SLOT2 may only be on if SLOT1 is.

Setting SHDN (bit 7 of 0x09) puts the part in a power-save state of 0.7 µA typical; registers keep their contents and stay readable and writable, and all interrupts are cleared. Both supplies may remain powered throughout. Setting RESET (bit 6) returns every register to its power-on value; the bit clears itself when the reset finishes, and it does not raise PWR_RDY.

operation.topic: Pulse width, resolution and sample rate
operation.text: LED_PW sets one pulse width for both LEDs and so the ADC integration time and resolution: 69 µs gives 15 bits, 118 µs 16 bits, 215 µs 17 bits, 411 µs 18 bits. A longer pulse caps the sample rate (Tables 11 and 12); if the rate written is too high for the pulse width, the part sets the highest rate that fits. One SpO2 sample is one red and one IR conversion.

LED1_PA (red) and LED2_PA (IR) each set an LED current from 0 to 50 mA in steps of about 0.2 mA, given enough VLED+ headroom. Individual parts can vary widely from the typical step values because of trimming.

INT goes low while any enabled interrupt is pending. A_FULL fires when the FIFO has only FIFO_A_FULL free slots left; PPG_RDY fires on each new FIFO sample; ALC_OVF fires when ambient cancellation runs out of range and ambient light reaches the ADC result; PWR_RDY fires when VDD rises through the undervoltage lockout at power-up or after a brownout; DIE_TEMP_RDY fires when a temperature conversion completes. Reading Interrupt Status 1 (0x00) clears A_FULL, PPG_RDY and ALC_OVF, and reading FIFO_DATA also clears PPG_RDY; reading Interrupt Status 2 (0x01) or TFRAC (0x20) clears DIE_TEMP_RDY. Reading a status register zeroes all its flags. Every source except PWR_RDY can be masked; PWR_RDY always stays enabled because a brownout resets the part, with all interrupts disabled, and the host needs to know. Unused enable bits are written 0.
INT is an open-drain output that may be pulled up to any supply up to +5 V. Its sink capability is small; a large pull-up, 4.7 kΩ for example, suits it.

The FIFO is circular and 32 samples deep. Each active LED channel stores 3 bytes per sample, so a SpO2 sample is 6 bytes and the FIFO holds 192 bytes. Data are left-justified: the MSB is always bit 17 of the 24-bit word, whatever the resolution, and bits 23 to 18 are unused (byte 1 carries FIFO_DATA[17:16], byte 2 [15:8], byte 3 [7:0]). In SpO2 mode the red triplet comes before the IR triplet of the same sample. The write pointer advances on each new sample; it can be written only in modes 010, 011 and 111. When the FIFO is full, new samples are dropped and OVF_COUNTER counts them, saturating at 0x1F and clearing when a sample is popped. With FIFO_ROLLOVER_EN set, a full FIFO wraps to zero and keeps filling with new data; with it clear, the FIFO stops updating until FIFO_DATA is read or a pointer is moved. SMP_AVE averages 1 to 32 adjacent samples per channel into one FIFO entry.

Before starting a SpO2 or HR run, zero the three pointer registers (0x04, 0x05 and 0x06) so the FIFO starts empty; the pointers also clear when VDD is cycled or falls below UVLO. To read: fetch FIFO_WR_PTR, work out the samples waiting (allowing for wrap), then burst-read FIFO_DATA (0x07), three bytes per active channel per sample, MSB byte first. The register address does not advance while FIFO_DATA is read, but the read pointer moves on once the first byte of a sample is read. To read a sample again after a bus error, write FIFO_RD_PTR back by one and read FIFO_DATA again. Of the FIFO registers, only FIFO_RD_PTR is normally written.

Writing TEMP_EN starts one die temperature conversion, which takes 29 ms typical; the bit clears itself when the result is ready. Resolution is 0.0625 °C. Read both TINT and TFRAC. The temperature is used to correct SpO2 for the shift of the red LED wavelength, to which the result is sensitive; the IR wavelength matters little. One temperature reading every one to a few seconds suffices. In HR mode temperature is not needed.

The LED die heats within tens of microseconds, so its wavelength follows the drive current. Estimate the LED temperature by adding the rise in Table 13 for the red LED current and duty cycle to the die temperature reading; this holds even for short pulses.

In SpO2 mode at 1000 sps with 69 µs pulses, the red LED is on for 69 µs and off for 931 µs, and the IR pulse follows the red pulse by 358 µs (end of one pulse to start of the next). Table 14 gives the spacing for each pulse width.

The 32-sample FIFO lets the host read in bursts rather than after every sample. In the SpO2 and HR timing examples the run of samples spans 15 ms to 300 ms. Tables 15 and 16 list the event order in SpO2 and HR modes.

The LEDs draw pulsed current at low duty cycle, which ripples VLED+. To keep the ripple out of the optical signal, the path from the source (battery, LDO or DC/DC converter) up to the pins must have resistance and inductance well under 1 Ω, with at least 1 µF of bypass to a solid ground plane placed as near the module as possible.

Bring up VDD before VLED+. SDA, SCL and INT may be pulled up to an external rail while the supplies are off. Once powered, the part raises PWR_RDY on INT; reading the interrupt status clears it. Any power-down order is tolerated.

Two-wire I2C/SMBus-compatible slave at up to 400 kHz. The 7-bit address is 0b1010111, so the write byte is 0xAE and the read byte 0xAF. SDA needs a pull-up, typically above 500 Ω; SCL is input only and needs a pull-up, typically above 500 Ω, when there are several masters or the master's SCL is open drain. Series resistors in SDA and SCL are optional; they protect the inputs from bus spikes and reduce crosstalk and undershoot. A STOP sent in the same SCL high period as a START is not recognised. The part acknowledges each byte written by holding SDA low in the ninth clock.

Write: slave ID with R/W = 0, register address, then one or more data bytes; the register pointer advances after each byte, so a whole bank can be written in one transfer, ended by STOP. Read: write the slave ID and register address, send a repeated START, then the slave ID with R/W = 1; the part sends from that register onward, advancing the pointer, until the master answers the last byte with NACK and a STOP. FIFO_DATA is the exception: the pointer stays on it, so reading the register after it needs a fresh address write. Reading past 0xFF does not wrap to 0x00 and returns no useful data.
